answer: Each identity claims one sun-exposure rack on a tundra mesa, locks a 70-credit bond, and mounts a pigment-dyed plate with a registered serial. Sunlight fades pigment along a published curve no lamp can fake. Each epoch the identity files its fade reading; an auditor re-measures the plate against the curve and sunlight spectrum within 3%; lamp-faded plates burn the bond. First rack costs 34 credits, the kth under one key 34+6(k-1), the 1000th 6,028; 1,000 fakes pay 3,031,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-lamp ring fails on the spectrum check. An honest agent pays 34 once and keeps it.
